pan_from_plate_quads.basis: mean lateral offset of the plate's back-edge midpoint vs front-edge midpoint over all M1 plate quads

pan_from_rubber.note: a nearer point on the mound-plate line shifting image-left means deeper points shift image-right (more negative plate_x); the implied term is far smaller than the measured x offset

critique.sign_convention_check: Correct. Field geometry: pitcher faces home with first base on his LEFT; the centre-field camera looks the same way, so image-left = first-base side, image-right = third-base side (where a RHB stands, matching the footage check). Statcast plate_x is from the catcher's view, positive to the catcher's right = first-base side = where a LHB stands. With u=0 at front_left (image-left) and x = -(17/12)(u-0.5): u=0 -> +0.708 ft (first-base side), u=1 -> -0.708 ft (third-base side). Consistent. n = e rotated to point up (negative image y) gives v positive above the ground line, and the matrix [[-17/12,0,17/24],[0,17/12,0],[0,0,1]] reproduces both formulas. Minor: the only sign-related trap is that front_left/front_right must be labelled in image coordinates (the note does), not from the catcher's perspective. The lateral chalk-line reference positions (inner +/-14.5 in = 1.208 ft, outer +/-62.5 in = 5.208 ft, spans 29 in and 125 in) are also correct.
critique.bias_estimate_check: Depth-parallax sign and nominal magnitude are right: a point d ft farther from the camera at height z projects at s*(d*sin(theta)+z*cos(theta)) px above the front-edge line, so z_mapped = z + d*tan(theta) (with c applied; d*sin(theta) with c=1 — same to 1%) -> +0.37 ft too HIGH for d=2.5, theta=8.5 deg. Scale-with-depth (0.6%) and cos(theta) (1.1% at 8.5 deg) are negligible as stated. What is understated: (1) theta is not known to 6-11 deg. sin(theta)=dy/(0.708*s), and the note's own back-corner rise spans 2.5-10 px across frames, which cannot be real tilt variation (the camera does not move), so the 4-px quantity carries ~+/-3 px of reading noise; honest range is theta ~ 4-15 deg, i.e. the parallax term is +0.17 to +0.68 ft at d=2.5 and the +/-2 px claim is optimistic. (2) Lateral parallax is ~2x understated: a 1-px lateral offset of the back-edge midpoint over the 0.708 ft * 38 px/ft = 27 px depth baseline is sin(phi)=0.037 -> phi ~2 deg, and the +/-1 px reading noise allows 0-4 deg -> d*sin(phi) = 0.09 ft nominal, up to 0.17 ft; one-signed, not 0.04 ft. Still below mitt reader noise but it is a bias, not noise. (3) Scale error from +/-2 px independently on BOTH ends is sqrt(2)*2/52 = 5.4%, not 4% (4% assumes one end only). (4) d is a per-pitch variable (catcher depth changes with count/pitch type by +/-0.5-1 ft), so the parallax bias has a +/-0.07-0.15 ft per-pitch spread on top of its mean; a single constant cannot remove it. (5) Reporting: a mapped plate_z carrying a known +4.5 in one-signed bias but labelled 'height above ground' is misleading; the bias is larger than the zone-edge precision the proxy is meant to deliver.

issues.title: Vertical scale (square pixels, vertical px/ft = lateral px/ft) is assumed, never measured, and the overlay evidence points the other way
issues.detail: Every z in the pipeline rests on vertical px/ft == lateral px/ft * cos(theta). The only vertical measurement in the note — the broadcast zone box at 46-48 px/ft against 36-40 px/ft lateral — contradicts that by 1.25-1.35x, and the pinhole argument used to dismiss it ('cannot happen for a planar rectangle') is itself conditional on square pixels, which is exactly the untested assumption. The mismatch is equally explained by (a) overlay semantics (e.g. a ball-radius-padded zone: +2.9 in total gives 1.96-2.11 ft -> 75-84 px at 38-40 px/ft, close to the 80-87 px observed) or (b) a pixel-aspect error in the frame extraction (anamorphic 1440x1080 source badly resampled), which would make all z's ~1.3x wrong. A 30% multiplicative z error (0.5-1.0 ft across the zone) is the same size as or larger than the parallax bias and is vertical-only, so nothing in the lateral chalk-line check can catch it. The overlay mismatch should be treated as an open defect, not a 'finding'.
issues.fix: Before any z is reported: (1) ffprobe the source/capture for sample_aspect_ratio and the resize chain; (2) in the end-to-end catch check, regress mapped z on reference z and report slope +/- CI and intercept +/- CI separately — a scale error shows as slope != 1, parallax as intercept != 0; choose catch frames to span the widest z range (include high balls and balls in the dirt) so slope SE ~ 0.38/(sqrt(n)*sd_z) is < 0.1; (3) if the slope is consistent with 1, the overlay can then be attributed to semantics and stated as such; otherwise fix the pixel aspect before v0 ships numbers.

issues.title: theta is read from a 4-px lever arm; the parallax bias range is understated and should not be given as 6-11 deg
issues.detail: sin(theta) = (back-corner rise)/(0.708 ft * 38 px/ft) = rise/27 px. The note's own data has that rise at 2.5-10 px across frames, which must be reading noise since the camera tilt is fixed, so theta is 4-15 deg, the parallax term at d=2.5 ft is +0.17 to +0.68 ft, and cos(theta) is 0.966-0.998 (up to 3.4%, not <=1.5%). The catch check will measure d*tan(theta) only as a lump; to transfer it to the setup frames you need theta and d separately.
issues.fix: Measure theta from a long ground baseline, not the plate's 8.5 in: the batter's box is 6 ft deep (front-to-back chalk lines ~34 px apart at 38 px/ft, +/-2 px -> theta to +/-0.5 deg), the catcher's box 8 ft, or the rubber-to-plate 60.5 ft in a wider shot (~340 px, with the 15% depth-scale correction). Likewise read phi from the rubber-vs-plate lateral offset (60.5 ft lever arm) instead of the 27-px plate depth. Report theta and phi with their propagated +/- and recompute the parallax range from them.

issues.title: Reported plate_z is 'height above ground' with a known +4-5 in one-signed bias left in; and the target quantity for the mitt is undefined (true mitt height vs plate-front-equivalent crossing height)
issues.detail: Two effects of the same size and opposite sign act on the mitt: parallax makes mapped z too high by d*tan(theta) ~ +0.15*d ft, while a ball that ends in the mitt has dropped |vz/vy|*d ~ 0.10*d (fastball, ~6 deg descent) to 0.21*d (curveball, ~12 deg) between the plate front and the mitt, so the true mitt is BELOW the plate-front crossing height by 0.25-0.5 ft. Uncorrected mapped z therefore happens to approximate the plate-front crossing height for fastballs and misses by ~0.15 ft for breaking balls, while being 0.37 ft off the true mitt height for all. The catch check, by evaluating the trajectory at mitt depth, measures pure parallax (correct for testing the mapping) — but if the downstream compares mitt z to sz_top/sz_bot (defined at the plate front), applying the parallax correction alone makes the proxy WORSE for fastballs. The note does not say which quantity plate_z of the mitt is meant to be.
issues.fix: State the target quantity explicitly in hop 2. If it is true mitt height: put the nominal offset into the affine translation term (z row = [0, 17/12, -d_nom*tan(theta)], still a constant 3x3) with d_nom=2.5 ft and the measured theta, and carry the residual range (+/-0.1-0.15 ft from d spread and theta error) as the uncertainty; do not label an uncorrected value 'height above ground'. If it is plate-front-equivalent crossing height: document that no correction is applied because parallax and ball drop roughly cancel, give the pitch-type-dependent residual (-0.1 to +0.15 ft), and name the field accordingly (e.g. plate_z_front_equiv_ft). Either way rename an uncorrected v0 output (z_image_plane_ft) rather than reporting it as feet above ground.

issues.title: Catch-frame check is biased toward the zone centre by framing motion and by the +/-0.15 s timing window
issues.detail: Frames at release+plateTime+{0.10,0.25,0.40} s with release +/-0.15 s means the 'earliest closed-mitt frame' can be anywhere from ~0 to ~0.4 s after the catch. Catchers begin the framing pull within ~0.1 s, moving the mitt several inches toward the zone centre; that is a systematic (toward-centre) error in both axes, not random spread, and it will shrink the measured parallax bias and inflate apparent accuracy at the zone edges. plateTime in the feed is measured from the y0=50 ft point, not release, adding ~0.03 s. Also, after closing, the mitt's visual centre is not the open-face centre read at setup (1-3 in offset), and the plate front edge is often occluded by the catcher/umpire at the catch so readers will be tempted to reuse the setup-frame corners, which is only valid if the camera did not zoom/pan during the pitch.
issues.fix: Sample every frame in [t_catch-0.2, t_catch+0.3] s and take the first frame in which the ball streak ends/disappears into the mitt (not the first 'closed-looking' frame among three fixed offsets); record the frame index used. Read the plate front edge (or, if occluded, two chalk-line intersections with known positions) in that same frame; flag any record where setup-frame corners were reused. Define 'mitt centre' once (pocket centre, where the ball sits) and use it for both setup and catch reads.

issues.title: The two numbers called rms_error_feet measure different things and neither is the error of the setup-mitt coordinate
issues.detail: The chalk-line check (crisp lines, +/-2-3 px, on-plane, d=0) measures only the lateral transform error (~0.05-0.1 ft) and will be mistaken for the lateral accuracy of the mitt coordinate, which is dominated by +/-10-15 px mitt reading (0.26-0.39 ft). The catch check measures parallax + reader noise on a closed mitt with the ball visible, a different and probably easier target than the open mitt at setup. rms also mixes bias and spread (rms^2 = bias^2 + SD^2), so a single rms hides a 0.37 ft bias behind reader noise. Overlay corners (if ever used) would be worse still: tautological laterally (width = plate width by construction), unknown semantics vertically, d=0 so no parallax, +/-1 px targets — not an estimate of mitt transform error.
issues.fix: Report per axis: transform error from chalk lines (bias, SD, n); end-to-end catch check (bias +/- SE, SD, slope/intercept, n_usable, n_skipped with reasons); reader repeatability for the SETUP mitt from the two-reader differences (SD = |diff|/sqrt(2)); assistant-vs-human difference on the verified subset. Give rms only as a derived number next to its components. Attach to each record a feet-domain uncertainty with components (reader px * ft/px; 5.4% scale * distance from origin; origin +/-0.05 ft; one-signed parallax range), not just a pixel +/- and a feet_per_pixel.

issues.title: Two-reader agreement estimates repeatability only; if both readers are assistant sessions it also shares their systematic errors
issues.detail: Agreement between two readers gives within-reader-type random spread (and with n=30 the SD has ~13% relative SE, fine), but it cannot see errors common to both: the mitt-centre definition, blur/compression, tendency to pick the glove's visual centroid vs the pocket, or a model-specific bias. Two sessions of the same model are not independent in the metrological sense. The '+/-10-15 px' is also undefined (1 sigma? max?), which changes every propagated feet number by ~2x.
issues.fix: Define the +/- as 1 sigma (or 95%) and keep it consistent. Use the human-verified subset as the accuracy anchor: at least 10 (prefer 15) setup frames and 10 catch frames read by the user, report assistant-minus-human mean and SD per axis; with sigma_diff ~0.3 ft, n=10 detects a 0.2 ft (8 px) reader bias at ~2 sigma. Two-reader agreement then reports repeatability, labelled as such.

issues.title: Sample size: 24 planned catch pitches (likely ~15-18 usable) resolves the vertical bias to only ~+/-0.1 ft (1 sigma) and the slope to ~+/-0.13
issues.detail: Per-pitch sigma ~ sqrt(0.35^2 reader + 0.1^2 reference depth + 0.1^2 scale) ~ 0.38 ft. Bias SE = 0.38/sqrt(n): 0.09 ft at n=18, 0.08 at n=24; 95% half-width +/-0.15-0.19 ft, i.e. a measured bias of 0.37 is clearly nonzero but is not known well enough to correct to zone-edge (1-2 in) precision. Resolving the bias to +/-0.1 ft at 95% needs ~55 usable pitches. Expected dropout (timing misses, occlusion, mitt moved, no release time) of 25-35% must be budgeted.
issues.fix: State n_usable and the resulting SE in the report, not just rms. Minimum honest set: >=18 usable catch pitches spanning high/low and fastball/breaking (to separate slope from intercept and to expose the pitch-type-dependent drop), >=30 setup frames for repeatability, >=10 human-verified in each. If the parallax offset is to be applied in v1, plan for ~50 catch pitches or accept +/-0.15 ft on the correction.

issues.title: Reference evaluation depth (y=-1.0 ft) and mitt depth both unknown per pitch; their effects add, not cancel
issues.detail: If the real mitt is 0.5 ft deeper than assumed, the reference z is ~0.07 ft lower (more drop, |vz/vy| ~0.14) AND the mapped z is ~0.07 ft higher (more parallax), so the measured bias shifts by ~0.15 ft per 0.5 ft of depth error. The sensitivity reported for y=-0.5/-1.5 covers only the reference half. Setup depth may also differ from catch depth (catchers often receive slightly in front of the setup point).
issues.fix: Report the combined sensitivity (reference + parallax) per 0.5 ft of depth, and where possible estimate per-frame depth from the catcher's knee/shin ground contact relative to the plate (image dy / (s*sin(theta)), using the better-measured theta). Record pitch type with each catch pitch since the drop term is pitch-type dependent.

issues.title: inside_annotated_quad (0<=u<=1, 0<=v<=1) is a 17x17 in square at ground level, not a zone test
issues.detail: With v in plate widths, v<=1 means below 17 in above ground; any downstream use as 'mitt inside zone' would be wrong. Harmless if it is a legacy field, misleading if consumed.
issues.fix: Rename to inside_plate_width_ground_square or drop it; do zone membership only in feet against sz_top/sz_bot after the depth/target-quantity decision above.

critique.sign_convention_check: Checked and CORRECT: (1) Statcast plate_x (GUMBO pitchData.coordinates.pX) is positive toward the catcher's right = first-base side = where a LHB stands; the 9P x0/vX0/aX use the same axis (sanity check: RHP x0 is negative, about -1.5 to -2.5 ft). (2) A centre-field camera sits behind the pitcher looking at home, so image-right = pitcher's right = third-base side = catcher's left = RHB side = negative plate_x. With u=0 at front_left (image-left), plate_x = -(17/12)(u-0.5) gives +0.708 ft at image-left: correct. (3) pX/pZ are defined where the ball crosses the FRONT of the plate, Statcast y = 17/12 ft from the back tip; the GUMBO 9P parameters are defined at y0 = 50 ft, z up, y positive toward the pitcher, so evaluating them at y = -1.0 ft (2.42 ft behind the front edge) is a valid extrapolation of a couple of feet. (4) Plate geometry: 17 in front edge, 8.5 in straight sides, 12 in sides meeting at the back point; back corners 17 in apart and 8.5 in behind the front edge; total depth 17 in: all as stated. The front edge faces the pitcher and is the lowest plate edge in a CF image: correct. (5) Batter's box: 4 ft x 6 ft, 6 in from the plate edge: inner line 14.5 in = 1.208 ft, outer line 62.5 in = 5.208 ft, spans 29 in and 125 in: correct. Two gaps to close: check 1 as written never tests the SIGN (it compares magnitudes to known positions). Add a per-PA sign test from the feed: GUMBO matchup.batSide (R/L) must coincide with the batter standing at u>1 for R and u<0 for L in the decision frame, and in check 2 the sign of (mapped mitt x) must match the sign of feed pX for pitches with |pX| > 0.5 ft. Also do not use GUMBO pitchData.coordinates.x/y (Gameday zone-image pixel coordinates, y downward) in place of pX/pZ. What is usable as ground truth: pX/pZ and the 9P trajectory (Hawk-Eye, cm-level), the plate dimensions, the box dimensions (subject to chalk condition), batSide. What is NOT: the broadcast overlay geometry, strikeZoneTop/strikeZoneBottom as image calibration, the umpire's call, and manual release_seconds at sub-0.1 s precision.
critique.bias_estimate_check: Depth-parallax formula and direction are right: a point d ft beyond the plate front at height z has image offset s[z cos(theta) + d sin(theta)] above the front-edge ground line, so the mapped height is z + d tan(theta), i.e. too HIGH; 2.5 ft x tan(8.5 deg) = 0.374 ft, and the quoted 0.16 to 0.68 ft is the correct span for d=1.5-3.5 ft and theta=6-11 deg. Two things are off. (a) The correct z conversion divides by cos(theta) rather than multiplying: v = z cos(theta)/(17/12), so z = (17/12) v / cos(theta); omitting it makes mapped z 1.1 percent too LOW, the opposite sign of what the note states (magnitude trivial, but the stated formula is wrong). (b) The theta range is not supported by the stated data: the 4 px plate-depth reading maps to sin(theta) = px/(0.708 x 38) = px/26.9, so the quoted 2.5-10 px spread corresponds to 5.3-21.8 deg, not 6-11 deg; theta is a camera constant (fixed mount, zoom does not change tilt), so use the median over all frames and treat the spread as reader noise, and better, estimate tan(theta) = (vertical bias of check 2)/d directly. The same reading noise kills the phi claim: a 1 px back-midpoint offset over the plate's 0.708 ft depth is already 2.1 deg, and +/-2 px corner noise gives +/-4 deg per frame, so phi is 0-5 deg unless the offset was averaged over all 30 frames; at phi = 4 deg the lateral parallax at d=2.5 ft is 0.17 ft, a systematic term, not negligible. Scale-with-depth (0.6 percent) and reader-noise numbers (10-15 px -> 0.26-0.39 ft at 38 px/ft; +/-2 px per end -> +/-4 percent scale) are arithmetically correct.

issues.title: Check 2 frame sampling will measure post-catch framing, not the catch
issues.detail: release_seconds is +/-0.15 s, which is +/-20 ft of ball flight and +/-4.5 frames at 29.97 fps (+/-9 at 59.94). The ball reaches the mitt about 0.02 s after plateTime, so the first sample at +0.10 s is nominally already 0.08 s after the catch and the +0.25/+0.40 s samples are well into the framing motion; when the timing error is negative all three samples are post-catch and the 'earliest closed-mitt frame' rule picks a framed position. Framing moves the mitt 0.1-0.25 ft toward the zone centre, so the resulting 'rms_error_feet' and bias are contaminated by a pitch-location-dependent shrinkage that looks like a scale error, and the reported lateral/vertical rms are not the mapping's error.
issues.fix: Extract every frame from nominal catch -0.25 s to +0.40 s and have readers find the first frame in which the ball is in the mitt (ball visible as a streak in the previous frame); record that frame index and the derived catch time. Report the catch-time residual vs release_seconds+plateTime as its own column; skip pitches where no pre-catch frame exists. Only then compute rms.

issues.title: Catch depth is unknown and differs from setup depth; the parallax 'calibration' is tied to d
issues.detail: Both the comparison (trajectory at y = -1.0 ft) and the bias term scale with d. Catchers receive the ball 1-2 ft in front of the set-up target (arm extended, one-knee stances catch low pitches near the back tip), so the catch depth is typically 1.4-2.4 ft behind the front edge while the setup mitt is 2.5-3.5 ft. The vertical bias measured in check 2 (d_catch tan theta) therefore does not transfer to the setup frames (d_setup tan theta); a 1 ft depth difference is 0.15 ft of z. The sensitivity at y = -0.5/-1.5 ft reports the trajectory side only, not the parallax side, and the two are correlated (same d).
issues.fix: Estimate d per frame from ground-contact points, which the ground plane resolves (5.7 px/ft depth scale): catcher's front shin-guard/knee or foot contact relative to the plate's front edge, +/-0.3 ft. Carry d_catch and d_setup per record; evaluate the trajectory at y = 17/12 - d_catch; report the bias as tan(theta) = bias/d_catch rather than as a fixed feet number, and in evidence state the expected setup-frame bias as d_setup tan(theta).

issues.title: phi is underdetermined; lateral depth parallax is not negligible
issues.detail: The back-edge midpoint lateral offset of ~1 px over a 0.708 ft plate depth implies phi = asin(1/26.9) = 2.1 deg, and the +/-1-2 px corner-reading noise makes any single-frame phi uncertain by +/-4 deg. Unless the 1 px is a 30-frame average, phi is anywhere in 0-5 deg, and at d = 2.5 ft the lateral shift is 0.04-0.22 ft, a systematic error of the same order as the reader noise. Broadcast CF cameras are often mounted several degrees off the mound-plate line.
issues.fix: Average the back-vs-front midpoint offset over all 30 decision frames (phi is a camera constant) and state the averaged value and its standard error; cross-check with the lateral bias from check 2, which equals d_catch tan(phi). Apply d tan(phi) as a signed correction if |phi| > 2 deg, otherwise list it with the actual range.

issues.title: theta from the 4 px plate reading is noise-dominated; 6-11 deg is not what the data say
issues.detail: sin(theta) = px/26.9 for a 38 px/ft frame: 2.5 px -> 5.3 deg, 4 px -> 8.5 deg, 10 px -> 21.8 deg. The stated 2.5-10 px spread therefore spans 5-22 deg, and the note quotes 6-11 deg without a derivation. Since tilt is fixed by camera height/distance, the per-PA spread is reader noise, not geometry.
issues.fix: Use the median across all frames for theta and report the spread as reader noise; prefer the check-2 estimate tan(theta) = vertical_bias/d_catch, and bound it with a camera-geometry sanity check (height/distance of the CF well). Report the parallax range with the theta range actually supported.

issues.title: Overlay refutation argument is wrong even though the conclusion is right
issues.detail: 'A pinhole cannot produce a 1.25-1.35x mismatch' assumes the overlay's height encodes the feed's 1.72-1.87 ft. If the overlay instead draws a generic or differently-sourced zone, 80-87 px at the lateral 36-40 px/ft is simply a 2.0-2.4 ft box (85/38 = 2.24 ft, e.g. a fixed 1.5-3.75 ft box, or zone plus ball-diameter padding), which is perfectly consistent with a planar rectangle at one depth. The right finding is that the overlay height is not the feed's strikeZoneTop/Bottom, not that the overlay is geometrically impossible.
issues.fix: Report the overlay as: width = plate width (consistent with lateral scale); implied height = height_px / s_lateral = 2.0-2.4 ft, inconsistent with the per-pitch feed zone (1.72-1.87 ft), hence overlay vertical edges carry no feed-derived information and cannot be used as sz ground truth. Keep the usable part: the overlay's vertical edges are a second reading of the plate's front-edge ends.

issues.title: inside_annotated_quad is always false for a mitt after the hop-1 change
issues.detail: With v in plate-width units, 0 <= v <= 1 means 0-17 in above the ground line. A setup mitt at 2-3 ft is v = 1.4-2.1, so any downstream use of inside_annotated_quad as a validity gate rejects every mitt record, and any use as a 'near the plate' flag is silently redefined.
issues.fix: Redefine the flag as lateral-only (0 <= u <= 1, with a stated vertical window such as 0 <= v <= 3 for plausibility) or rename it to in_plate_width and add a separate height_plausible flag; record the definition in the hop-1 evidence.

issues.title: Plate corners are usually occluded in catch frames
issues.detail: At the catch the catcher's mitt, shin guards, umpire and dust frequently cover the front edge of the plate, especially on low pitches. Reading W and front_left in that frame, as the plan requires, will have far larger error than the +/-2 px assumed, and the error is correlated with pitch height (low pitches = worse occlusion), biasing the vertical rms.
issues.fix: Reuse the decision-frame plate reading of the same pitch when the framing is unchanged (verify with two fixed landmarks, e.g. the inner box lines or an on-screen graphic position); if framing changed, mark the record as plate_unreadable and exclude it from rms rather than guessing.

issues.title: Parallax bias and in-flight drop have opposite signs and must not be netted
issues.detail: Between the plate front (where pZ is defined) and the mitt the ball drops vZ x (2.4 ft / ~130 ft/s) = 0.15-0.36 ft (vZ -8 to -20 ft/s), while the mapping reads the mitt ~0.37 ft too high. A naive comparison of mapped setup-mitt z with pZ would show a small residual and could be reported as 'small error' when it is two cancelling systematics of 0.2-0.4 ft each. Lateral movement over the same distance (vX x 0.018 s) is 0.05-0.1 ft.
issues.fix: In the per-record evidence keep three separate signed terms: depth-parallax bias (d tan theta), trajectory evaluation depth (y used), and any downstream mitt-vs-plate-front comparison; never report a single netted vertical offset.

issues.title: The ball sits in the pocket, not at the visual mitt centre
issues.detail: A catcher's mitt is ~10-11 in across; the ball is held in the web/pocket, offset 1-3 in (0.1-0.25 ft) from the visible mitt centre toward the thumb/web side, consistently per catcher. In check 2 this is a systematic lateral (and some vertical) offset attributed to the mapping.
issues.fix: Have readers mark the ball (or the pocket) in catch frames, not the mitt centre; report the mean signed mitt-centre-minus-ball offset per catcher as a separate term if both are read.

issues.title: z formula uses cos(theta) in the wrong direction
issues.detail: The image vertical extent of a vertical segment is h cos(theta) times the lateral scale, so h = (17/12) v / cos(theta); the note's (17/12) v cos(theta) has the correction the wrong way. Effect is 1.1 percent at 8.5 deg (0.03 ft at z = 2.5 ft), but the stated formula and the stated sign of the omitted effect are wrong.
issues.fix: Write plate_z = (17/12) v / cos(theta); state 'omitted: mapped z is 1-2 percent too low' in evidence.

issues.title: Check 1 line-width convention and chalk condition
issues.detail: Box lines are 2-4 in wide (0.17-0.33 ft, 6-12 px at 38 px/ft); reading the line centre vs the rulebook edge is a +/-0.1-0.17 ft systematic that would dominate a lateral rms otherwise expected around 0.1 ft. Inner lines at the plate-front row are scuffed by batters' feet and often unreadable by mid-game, and the plate's beveled black border (about 0.75 in per side, 2-3 px) must be excluded from W.
issues.fix: Specify that readers mark the plate-side edge of each chalk line and the white/black boundary of the plate, report line readability per frame, and exclude unreadable lines rather than interpolating.

issues.title: Ground-truth inventory for strikeZoneTop/Bottom
issues.detail: GUMBO pitchData.strikeZoneTop/strikeZoneBottom are per PITCH (they vary within a PA in the Hawk-Eye era), in feet above ground on the same vertical axis as pZ, derived from the batter's tracked stance (pre-2020 they were operator-set per batter/PA). They are not a physical landmark in the frame and are defined for the plate-front plane, where the batter does not stand, so they cannot calibrate pixels and cannot be read off the image; the note already does not use them, which is right.
issues.fix: State this explicitly in the evidence so no later hop uses sz_top/sz_bot or the overlay as a vertical scale; the only vertical ground truth is the ball (pZ at y = 17/12, or the 9P trajectory at the mitt depth).

issues.title: Depth-parallax term belongs in the hop-2 matrix; leaving it out knowingly biases every plate_z by ~+0.3-0.4 ft
issues.detail: The note derives the bias correctly (a ground-level point d ft behind the plate front projects d*sin(theta) higher, read as d*tan(theta) of height) and then declines to apply it on the grounds that v0 is 'the geometric matrix'. But d*tan(theta) IS geometry, not a fit: with d=2.4 ft (Statcast y=-1) and theta=8.5 deg it is +0.36 ft, larger than the reader-noise rms (0.26-0.39 ft) and about one fifth of the zone height. Every reported mitt plate_z is therefore too high by roughly a third of a foot while the lateral axis is unbiased, so any downstream 'mitt above/below zone edge' statistic is shifted by ~4 in. Keeping the matrix 'pure' and documenting the bias in evidence does not make the reported coordinates less misleading. Note also that in the implementation as written (c=1, no depth-scale term) the net bias at z=2.5 ft is ~+0.33 ft, not +0.37, because the ignored cos(theta) term (-0.03 ft) and depth-scale term (-0.015 ft) are both negative.
issues.fix: Use the full geometric affine: z row = [0, (17/12)*cos(theta), -d0*tan(theta)] with d0 = 2.4 ft (y=-1) and theta from a proper estimate (see theta issue). Carry sigma(d0)=+/-0.5 ft and sigma(theta) into the uncertainty, and let check 2 verify that the residual mean offset is ~0 rather than ~+0.37. Keep the 'uncorrected' numbers only as a diagnostic column.

issues.title: Tilt theta from a 4-px quad is far less certain than '+/- a few degrees'; the measured 2.5-10 px spread implies theta anywhere from 5 to 24 deg
issues.detail: sin(theta) = rise_px / (0.708 ft * s). With s~36.7 px/ft: 2.5 px -> 5.5 deg, 4 px -> 8.9 deg, 10 px -> 22.9 deg. A fixed CF camera does not retilt by 17 deg between PAs, so the spread is reader noise/occlusion (shin guards, dirt, the plate's bevel), and it is +/-3 px not +/-1-2 px; worse, a reader bias of 1-2 px on where the 'back corner' is does not average out over 30 frames. The parallax bias scales with tan(theta), so the honest bias range from this data alone is +0.16 to +1.0 ft (d=1.5-3.5, theta=5-23 deg), not +0.16-0.68. The 4-px quantity is the single weakest number in the note and it drives the dominant systematic.
issues.fix: Estimate theta from a long depth baseline, once for the camera, not per frame: (a) add the plate apex to the annotation (front edge to apex = 17 in, doubling the lever to ~8 px); (b) the batter's-box 6-ft side lines (6 ft * s * sin(theta) ~ 34 px, read to +/-2 px -> theta to +/-8%) or the catcher's-box 8-ft lines in early-inning frames; (c) if the rubber is visible, rubber width (24 in) vs plate width gives camera distance D and the rubber-plate vertical separation gives theta jointly. Pool across frames; report theta +/- sigma and propagate into the parallax term.

issues.title: Horizontal off-axis angle phi is underestimated by 2x and its uncertainty is ~+/-4 deg, making the x-parallax bias up to ~0.25 ft, not 0.04 ft
issues.detail: A point 0.708 ft deeper shifts laterally by s*0.708*tan(phi) ~ 26 px per radian, so a 1-px midpoint offset is phi ~2.2 deg, not '~1 deg or less'. Each midpoint is the mean of two +/-2 px corner reads, so the front-back midpoint difference has ~+/-2 px noise -> phi uncertain by ~+/-4.4 deg. CF cameras are routinely several degrees off the rubber-plate line. At phi=5 deg, d=2.5 ft the mitt's mapped plate_x is biased by 0.22 ft in one consistent direction, comparable to the reader noise and large enough to flip inside/outside calls near the edge. Check 1 (ground chalk lines) cannot see this because the lines are on the plate-front row (d=0).
issues.fix: Measure phi from a long lever: the image-column offset between the rubber centre and the plate-front midpoint is ~s*b*60.5/(D-60.5) ~ 45-50 px per degree of camera azimuth (b = D*tan(phi)), so one frame with both visible pins phi to ~0.1 deg; otherwise use the plate apex (17-in depth lever, ~1 px/deg). Add -d0*tan(phi) to the x row of the matrix with its sign fixed by which side of the rubber-plate line the camera sits (from the rubber-offset read), and propagate sigma(phi).

issues.title: The 1.25-1.35x overlay/plate scale mismatch must be resolved, not shelved: one of the two numbers is wrong by 25-35% and it is the vertical scale
issues.detail: The note is right that a pinhole camera gives vertical scale = s*cos(theta) <= s for a frontal rectangle, so a calibrated overlay cannot be 1.3x taller. But the two remaining explanations have opposite consequences: (1) the broadcast box is not geometrically registered or does not use the feed's sz values (note: the quoted 80 px/1.72 ft and 87 px/1.87 ft are both 46.5 px/ft, i.e. the box height tracks the per-batter zone, which argues against a 'generic' box); or (2) the readers' plate width is ~25% too narrow (dirt-covered edges, 'visible white' not the 17-in edge), in which case s is really ~46 px/ft and every reported foot value (lateral, vertical, reader-noise feet, parallax feet) is 25% too large. 'Reported as a finding' leaves the vertical scale unverified. Square pixels are safe for a 1280x720 grab from any 1080 source (1440/1280x1080 anamorphic sources resample to square at 1280x720), and distortion is negligible for a ~14,700-px focal length over a 100-px span, so neither of those rescues the overlay; it is the plate width or the overlay.
issues.fix: Gate hop 2 on check 1: the batter's-box 48-in width and the 125-in outer-to-outer span distinguish s=37 (382 px) from s=46.5 (484 px) unambiguously; run it before any feet are reported. Confirm SAR=1:1 with ffprobe on the source. In check 2, regress mapped mitt z on trajectory z (errors in both -> Deming/orthogonal fit) and report slope and intercept separately: slope != 1 is a scale error (fix the matrix), intercept is parallax. The current plan ('mean signed offset') would silently fold a 30% scale error into 'bias'.

issues.title: Per-frame rotation of e from a 50-px segment adds ~+/-0.13 ft lateral error at mitt height that is not in the error budget
issues.detail: With +/-2 px on each front-edge end, the direction of e has ~2.8/52 = 0.054 rad (3 deg) noise. The mitt is ~90 px above the edge, so u picks up 0.054*90 ~ 5 px = 0.13 ft of vertical-into-lateral leakage, same size as the stated scale error and avoidable. The same +/-2 px on W gives +/-5.5% per-frame scale (sqrt(2)*2/52), not +/-4%, while the note itself says zoom is constant within a PA. Camera roll is a constant of the camera, not a per-frame quantity.
issues.fix: Estimate roll once (pool e across all frames, or from the long chalk/overlay lines) and use that fixed rotation in hop 1; use the per-PA mean W for scale (per-frame only if the zoom visibly changes). Add the residual rotation term to the lateral error budget.

issues.title: Check 2 frame sampling (+0.10/+0.25/+0.40 s with +/-0.15 s timing) will often read a post-impact, framed mitt and bias the vertical/lateral offsets toward the zone centre
issues.detail: The catch is ~0.02 s after plate crossing, so with the timing slack the earliest sampled frame can be 0.2+ s after impact. The mitt recoils 2-6 in on impact and framing moves it toward the zone within 0.1-0.2 s, pulling low pitches up and edge pitches in. That bias correlates with pitch location, so it inflates the apparent +z bias on low pitches and shrinks it on high ones, and corrupts the slope test. The sensitivity scan over y=-0.5/-1.5 does not cover this.
issues.fix: Grab every frame from t_nom-0.20 to +0.30 s, record the chosen frame's offset, and read the mitt in the first frame where the ball streak terminates at the mitt (or the last frame with the ball 1-2 ft in front of it). Exclude frames where the mitt has visibly moved from the pre-impact position and report the count excluded.

issues.title: State which depth the reported plate_z refers to; parallax and ball drop between plate front and mitt partly cancel for the intended comparison
issues.detail: The ball drops 0.2-0.35 ft between the plate front (y=1.417) and the mitt (y=-1): vZ at the plate is ~11-15 ft/s (VAA -5 to -8 deg at 110-125 ft/s) over 0.019-0.022 s. Check 2 handles this correctly by evaluating the trajectory at the mitt depth, so the +0.37 ft parallax is the right bias for 'true mitt height'. But if the proxy is then compared with pZ or sz_top/sz_bot (defined at the plate front), the relevant offset is parallax minus drop, i.e. roughly 0 to +0.15 ft, and applying the parallax correction alone would move the setup mitt ~0.2-0.3 ft below the plate-front-equivalent target. Currently the note's numbers are 'accidentally' closer to plate-front-equivalent than corrected ones would be, which will confuse any consumer.
issues.fix: Define plate_z explicitly as mitt height at the catcher's depth (y=-1), apply the parallax correction, and add a separate documented term for comparing with plate-front quantities (expected drop by pitch type from the feed's trajectory, 0.2-0.35 ft) rather than letting the two effects cancel implicitly.

issues.title: Catch-depth != setup-depth is asserted, not measured
issues.detail: Catchers receive deeper than they set up, especially on low/breaking pitches (receive at y ~ -1.5 to -2 vs set-up at y ~ -0.5 to -1). A 0.5-1 ft depth difference changes the parallax by 0.07-0.15 ft, so check 2 can over-estimate the setup-mitt bias by that amount.
issues.fix: Have readers also mark the catcher's front foot/knee or the mitt's apparent size in setup vs catch frames to bound the depth change, or at least report the bias with the y=-0.5/-1.5 sensitivity as an explicit range on the setup-mitt correction rather than a single number.

issues.title: front_left/front_right must be defined as IMAGE-left/right, otherwise the sign flips
issues.detail: The minus sign in plate_x = -(17/12)(u-0.5) is correct only if front_left is the image-left end (first-base side from the CF camera). If any annotator labelled corners in field terms (catcher's left = third base = image right), every x sign flips. The note's RHB-on-image-right check will catch it only if it is actually run per annotation batch.
issues.fix: Enforce in code: front_left.x < front_right.x in image coordinates (swap if not), and assert n.y < 0 (image up) after rotating e. Run the RHB/LHB side check on every frame using the feed's batter handedness and fail the record on mismatch.

issues.title: inside_annotated_quad is meaningless for the mitt and should not be reported as is
issues.detail: 0<=v<=1 means 'within 17 in of the ground', which a 2-3 ft mitt never satisfies; the flag will be false for essentially every record while its name suggests 'over the plate'.
issues.fix: Drop it or redefine as lateral-only (0<=u<=1) and rename accordingly.

issues.title: cos(theta) is a known, signed, free correction; apply it
issues.detail: c=0.989 at 8.5 deg is -0.03 ft at z=2.5 ft, always in the same direction. Omitting a known systematic to keep the matrix 'clean' is not justified when the matrix is constant anyway.
issues.fix: Use (17/12)*cos(theta) in the z row with theta from the improved estimate.

critique.sign_convention_check: Correct. Statcast plate_x is positive toward the catcher's right (first-base side, LHB side). The CF camera faces the catcher, so the catcher's right is image-left: image-right = third-base side = RHB side = negative plate_x, hence plate_x = -(17/12)(u-0.5) with u=0 at the image-left end of the front edge. The vertical direction n = e rotated to point to negative image y is correct and world-vertical lines are image-vertical to better than 1 part in 10^4 (nadir vanishing point at ~f/tan(theta) ~ 10^5 px). The only sign hazard is that 'front_left' is nowhere stated to be image-left; enforce it in code and run the RHB-on-image-right check on every frame using feed handedness.
critique.bias_estimate_check: Formulas are right: depth-segment foreshortening ratio = sin(theta), vertical-line scale = s*cos(theta), ground-point parallax = d*tan(theta) read as height (too HIGH, correct sign). Magnitudes recomputed: s = 52 px / 1.417 ft = 36.7 px/ft (note's 38 corresponds to 54 px; immaterial). sin(theta) = 4/(0.708*36.7) = 0.154 -> theta = 8.9 deg (note: 8-9, OK). Parallax: 2.5*tan(8.5 deg) = 0.374 ft (note +0.37, OK); range 1.5*tan6 = 0.158 to 3.5*tan11 = 0.680 ft (note 0.16-0.68, arithmetically right but the theta range is understated: the observed 2.5-10 px rise spread implies theta 5-23 deg, i.e. bias up to ~1.0 ft until theta is measured from a longer baseline). Net bias in the implementation as written (c=1, no depth-scale term) at z=2.5 ft is ~+0.33 ft rather than +0.37, since the two neglected terms are -0.03 and -0.015 ft. x-parallax: 0.708 ft of depth shifts 26 px/rad laterally, so 1 px -> phi ~2.2 deg, not <=1 deg, and the midpoint read noise gives +/-4 deg; d*tan(phi) is up to ~0.2-0.25 ft, not 0.04. Scale-with-depth 2.5/400 = 0.6% correct and negligible. Reader-noise conversions (10-15 px -> 0.27-0.41 ft; +/-2 px ends -> scale +/-5.5% not 4%; origin +/-0.05 ft) essentially right. Missing from the budget: rotation noise of e (~+/-0.13 ft lateral at mitt height), post-impact framing motion in check 2, catch-vs-setup depth difference (0.07-0.15 ft), and the unresolved 25-35% overlay/plate scale question, which, if the plate width is the wrong one, scales every number here by 0.75-0.8. Lens distortion (telephoto, ~14,700 px focal length, 100-px span) and the square-pixel assumption for a 1280x720 grab are safely negligible; the note is right to ignore them.
